title: feat(011sk6): (0,1,1) same-k reverse fails at k=6: t=10 vs t=18
science: Discriminator between the two reversers: at same-k k=6 on B_18(0), (0,1,1) FAILS (t(6,0,0)=10, t(6,6,6)=18, so 300 < 324) while nu on the same host and same comparator HOLDS (432>400, #6782). So the seed-exit clause is what keeps nu's same-k reverse alive at k=6, and the cheaper rule loses it -- the rules are separable at this scale, not interchangeable. Records the axis crossover again: t(6,0,0)=10 < axis-skeleton sum 16.
